sa→C Backend > sa2c Performance Comparison: C / JS / Interpreter

sa2c Performance Comparison: C / JS / Interpreter (2026-10-16)

Question: how well do programs generated by sa→C actually run? The conclusion up front: C(-O2) is about an order of magnitude faster than JS (10~20x), and about three orders of magnitude faster than the interpreter; compiled products are 70~90% smaller than the old backend's; millisecond-scale small demos are in the same tier on every backend (startup noise dominates). The method follows this site's convention (medians, tier verdicts).

1. Method and Environment

  • Machine: an AMD EPYC 7B12 container, 8 cores, 51GB memory; cc is GCC 13.3.0, the C side uniformly uses -std=c99, comparing -O2 / -O0; node v20.19.0, bun 1.4.3.
  • Workloads: 3 self-written benches (Appendix A, full text below; not repo files) — bench_sum (i64 accumulation, 2 million iterations), bench_fadd (f64 accumulation, 2 million iterations), bench_fib (recursive fib(25)=75025, call-intensive). All three self-verify their output.
  • C uses -DSA_GAS_LIMIT=50000000ULL (with the default 10,000 units, a 200-thousand-iteration loop immediately hits an out of gas trap; see §4; benches need a larger limit); JS uses the sa build-js default format; the interpreter is sa run.
  • C/JS take the median of 5 runs; the interpreter is too slow and was run only once (startup cost is included, on the same basis for every backend).

2. Run Times (Milliseconds)

benchC -O2C -O0nodebunInterpreter
sum, 2 million iterations4196845≈4000 (single run)
fadd, 2 million iterations4406438≈4000 (single run)
fib(25) recursive254331≈41000 (single run)

Reading: C(-O2) ≈ 10~20x JS (consistent for loop- and call-intensive workloads); the interpreter is about 1000x slower (recursive fib reaches 20000x, dominated by call overhead). -O0 is 2~10x slower than -O2, which is the usual cc optimization effect and has nothing to do with the emitter. Millisecond-scale small demos (such as fib(8)) are at the 1ms level on every backend, with process startup noise dominating — look only at the tier.

3. Compiled Products: the New Backend Is 70~90% Smaller Than the Old Backend

demoOld lines / statics / bytesNew lines / statics / bytes
01_hello_world180 / 120 / 1506543 / 8 / 1758
466_callback_register_invoke228 / 122 / 16269135 / 27 / 5810
302_http_server (including 13 bindings + the state table)— (no old counterpart)240 / 52 / 14522

Everything that shrank is dead code (unused helpers, unreachable functions, uncalled extern stubs), and behavior was confirmed unchanged across the full 936-demo differential. At runtime, small demos are in the same tier old vs new (within noise).

4. Gas Notes (Measured)

  • With the default SA_GAS_LIMIT=10000, a 200-thousand-iteration loop demo directly reports [sa-trap] out of gas (exit=1): each function entry + each label deducts 1 unit, so a large loop must enlarge the limit with -DSA_GAS_LIMIT=…. This is a parameter that must be decided before going live (see 02_runtime).
  • A check itself is about 2 ALU/memory-access instructions and cannot be separated from noise at the 2-million scale, so it was not quantified separately; the -O2 vs -O0 gap comes entirely from cc optimization and has nothing to do with Gas.

5. Honest Disclaimers

  • The C-side numbers include process startup (a significant share in millisecond-scale benches); cross-tier conclusions (10x/1000x) are unaffected, and decimals within the same tier are not comparable.
  • The interpreter numbers are single runs; the bench programs live in /tmp (not repo files), with the full text in Appendix A, reproducible with the same commands (--project-root points at the sci source tree to resolve sa_std).
  • The old backend's products come from the repository's tracked demos/c/*/main.c (the version before the sa-c branch merge).

6. sa-c vs the Native Backend: Same Workloads, Measured (Added 2026-10-16)

The C/JS/interpreter numbers above are benches from the sa-c branch. After merging into main (the zig 0.17 tree, sa 0.1.6), the same benches from Appendix A were used to additionally measure the native LLVM backend ( sa build-exe with default optimization, on the same AMD EPYC 7B12 container, median of 5 runs, milliseconds):

benchC -O2Native LLVMC -O0nodebunInterpreter
sum, 2 million iterations46.9196845≈4000 (single run)
fadd, 2 million iterations410.9406438≈4000 (single run)
fib(25) recursive22.954331≈41000 (single run)

Reading: the native backend and C(-O2) are in the same tier (loop-intensive workloads 1.2~2.7x slower, call-intensive ones tied); the native backend is about 6~15x faster than JS and 3~4 orders of magnitude faster than the interpreter. In other words, in this merge sa-c has no regression to speak of — it stepped directly onto the tier that previously only the native backend occupied, while JS/the interpreter remain in their original tiers (compare this site's 14_zig017_perf peer conclusions: on workloads such as b64 the tier gap between native and wasm/JS stayed consistent before and after the merge). Millisecond-scale benches include startup noise; look only at the tier, not the decimals.

Appendix A: Full Text of the Bench Programs

@import "sa_std/io/print.sai"
@const OUT = utf8:"ok\n"
// bench_sum：sum 0..N-1，N=2000000 -> 1999999000000
@main() -> i32:
L_ENTRY:
    n = 2000000 as i64
    one = 1 as i64
    i = 0 as i64
    acc = 0 as i64
    jmp L_LOOP
L_LOOP:
    c = slt i, n
    br c -> L_BODY, L_DONE
L_BODY:
    acc = add acc, i
    i = add i, one
    !c
    jmp L_LOOP
L_DONE:
    !c
    !n
    !one
    !i
    expect = 1999999000000 as i64
    ok = eq acc, expect
    !acc
    !expect
    br ok -> L_OK, L_ERR
L_OK:
    !ok
    call @sa_print_bytes(&OUT, 3)
    return 0
L_ERR:
    !ok
    return 1
// bench_fadd：0.5 累加 2000000 次 == 1000000.0（fdiv/sitofp/fptrunc 建值）
@main() -> i32:
L_ENTRY:
    zero_i = 0 as i32
    one_i = 1 as i32
    two_i = 2 as i32
    n = 2000000 as i64
    one_64 = 1 as i64
    zero_f = sitofp zero_i as f64
    one_f = sitofp one_i as f64
    two_f = sitofp two_i as f64
    half = fdiv one_f, two_f
    acc = sitofp zero_i as f64
    i = 0 as i64
    jmp L_LOOP
L_LOOP:
    c = slt i, n
    br c -> L_BODY, L_DONE
L_BODY:
    acc = fadd acc, half
    i = add i, one_64
    !c
    jmp L_LOOP
L_DONE:
    !c
    !n
    !one_64
    !i
    !half
    tmp = 1000000 as i64
    exp2 = sitofp tmp as f64
    ok = fcmp_eq acc, exp2
    !tmp
    !exp2
    !acc
    br ok -> L_OK, L_ERR
L_OK:
    !ok
    call @sa_print_bytes(&OUT, 3)
    return 0
L_ERR:
    !ok
    return 1
// bench_fib：fib(25) == 75025（递归，调用密集）
@fib(n: i32) -> i32:
L_ENTRY:
    base = sle n, 1
    br base -> L_BASE, L_REC
L_BASE:
    !base
    return n
L_REC:
    !base
    n1 = sub n, 1
    n2 = sub n, 2
    a = call @fib(n1)
    b = call @fib(n2)
    sum = add a, b
    !n
    !a
    !b
    return sum

@main() -> i32:
L_ENTRY:
    result = call @fib(25)
    expect = 75025 as i32
    ok = eq result, expect
    !result
    !expect
    br ok -> L_OK, L_ERR
L_OK:
    !ok
    call @sa_print_bytes(&OUT, 3)
    return 0
L_ERR:
    !ok
    return 1

Sources: an AMD EPYC 7B12 container, C -O2/-O0 (GCC 13.3, GAS_LIMIT=50000000ULL) median of 5 runs; node v20.19.0 / bun 1.4.3 (build-js default format) median of 5 runs; the interpreter, single runs. Old products: the main.c tracked in sci/sa-c.
